title: Say hello to Pocket
prompt: Write a two-line program. First log the text `Welcome to Pocket`. Then log the total of three expenses, `450`, `1200` and `899`, by letting JavaScript do the addition inside `console.log()`.
hints: Text goes inside quotes, `"like this"`. Numbers do not need quotes.
You can put a whole calculation inside the parentheses, for example `console.log(1 + 2)`.
explanation: The engine runs your two statements in order. In the first, `"Welcome to Pocket"` is text, so it is printed as it is. In the second, JavaScript evaluates `450 + 1200 + 899` first, gets `2549`, and only then hands that single number to `console.log()`. Working out what is inside the parentheses before using it is a rule you will lean on in every lesson.

checks.welcome-first: Logs the welcome before the total
